sections.title: 3.4.3 Echocardiography
sections.content: Mentions studies and advancements in echocardiography techniques for congenital heart defects, emphasizing intraoperative use and transesophageal echocardiography.

sections.title: 3.4.4 CMR Imaging
sections.content: Discusses the use of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging to assess heart structure, function, and blood flow in congenital heart disease patients. It also mentions studies focusing on the use of CMR to evaluate right ventricular volume, mass, and ejection fraction, as well as stress testing and late gadolinium enhancement techniques.

sections.title: 3.4.5 Cardiac Computed Tomography
sections.content: Highlights the use of CT imaging in assessing congenital heart disease, mentioning potential radiation risks and the use of second-generation scanners for noninvasive coronary artery assessment.

sections.title: 3.4.6 Cardiac Catheterization
sections.content: Details the procedural aspects and safety concerns associated with cardiac catheterization in children and adolescents, emphasizing risk assessment and the prediction of risks related to interventional procedures.

sections.title: 3.4.7 Exercise Testing
sections.content: Covers the importance of exercise testing in congenital heart disease for assessing exercise intolerance and its association with morbidity, emphasizing its use in clinical evaluations.

sections.title: 3.5 Transition Education
sections.content: Discusses the importance of transition education for adolescents with congenital heart disease, aiming to improve knowledge, self-management, and outcomes.
